caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 422 of 2010
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Principal and Secretary, Nawabgonj Government College, Nawabgonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahabuba Khatun (Dolly) and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 05.02.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 dismissing the suit. The plaintiff-respondent herein filed the above mentioned Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 for declaration of title and partition. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that 4.02 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint originally belonged to 3 brothers, namely, Ashutosh Chatyapadhya, Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya and Monimdra Chatyapadhya in equal share and the C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. That after partition of Pakistan and India Sharat Chandra Migrated to India and arranged an exchange of his share i.e. .95 acre out of schedule 'Ka' land with Indian land of one Ishahaque Mia-the father of the plaintiffs. That for effecting the exchange Sharat Chandra executed a power of attorney in favour of one Harun-ar-Rashid. Harun-ar-Rashid having obtained necessary permission from the then District Collector, Rajshahi, executed and registered a deed of exchange dated 13.10.1952 in favour of Ishahaque Mia. Thus Ishahaque Mia having acquired title and possession in the suit land had been in possession and enjoyment of the same for long 20 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants, Nawabgonj Government College and others. That Ishahaque Mia while in possession of the suit land executed a power of attorney in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid who being so empowered executed and registered two hiba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 09.10.1974 transferring the said .94 acre of land of Ishahaque Mia in favour of his daughters, the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4. Thus the plaintiffs acquired the suit land and since acquisition they have been in possession of the same by paying rent to the government to the knowledge of all including the defendants. That the defendant college subsequently purchased 2/3rd share of 'Ka' schedule land from Ashutosh and Monindra and has been in ejamali possession of that land with Ishahaque Mia and thereafter with the plaintiffs. That the 'Ka' schedule land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds among these co-sharers. That only in the month of October, 1985 when an employee of the plaintiffs went to pay rent in the local Tahsil Office the Tahsildar disclosed that the land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 College in R.S. Khatian and was finally published. That this R.S. record of the land in the name of the college in 16 annas share is wrong and collusive. That on the basis of this wrong recording the defendant college claimed title in the entire 'Ka' schedule land and thus the title of the plaintiffs in the suit has been clouded and hence the suit. 

 2. The defendant college and the government contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants admit the title of 3 C.S. recorded tenants and subsequently also of Ishahaque Mia in the 'Ka' schedule land. But their case is that the defendant college being established in the then newly created Nawabgonj Sub-Division purchased 95 1/2 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule from Ashutosh Chattapadhya by a registered sale deed dated 23.02.1957 and also purchased the other 95 1/2 decimals of land from Monindra Chatyapadhya Chandra by registered sale deed dated 12.04.1957. That the share of Sharat Chandra was transferred to Ishahaque Mia by way of exchange and the said Ishahaque Mia transferred his 95 1/2 decimals of land to the college by an oral gift in presence of many and the college authority accepted it with gratitude. These defendants stated also that out of 4.02 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint 2.86 acres of land only finally stood as rest 1.16 acres fell into road and ditches. That the college authority thus, is in possession of 2.86 acres of land of the 'Ka' schedule to the knowledge of all including the plaintiffs. This land has been duly recorded in the name of the college in R.S. khatian. The college authority has erected wall on the west and northern side of the R.S. plot few years ago. The college authority is in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years and as such they have acquired title by adverse possession also. That the plaintiffs have filed this suit on false claim suppressing the real facts. 

 4. On appeal the High Court Division set aside the findings and decision of the trial court and decreed the suit making observations and findings to the effect that the plaintiffs being daughters of the admitted co-sharers have succeeded in proving their title to the extent of 1/3rd share in the land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint and that the defendants could not prove their claim that the father, of the plaintiffs transferred his 1/3rd share in the 'Ka' schedule land in favour of the defendant college by oral gift and that the defendant college could not prove also its claim that the college has acquired title in this land by adverse possession also and that the recording of the 'Ka' schedule land in the name of the defendant college in 16 annas in R.S. Khatian has been wrong.
